# Model ensembles

Advice is increasingly based on an ensemble of assessment models that span structural uncertainty (natural
mortality, steepness, growth, data weighting). `ss3_ensemble()` combines the MVLN draws of several SS3 runs, as
`ss3diags::SSdeltaMVLN(weight = )` with `SSplotEnsemble(joint = TRUE)`: each model contributes draws in proportion
to its weight, and the joint ensemble pools them. Ratios to the targets are computed within each model, with its
own reference points, before pooling. `ss3plot_ensemble()` shows the models in colour and the joint ensemble in
black, with `ss3plot_trj()`.

The example is the ICES Central Baltic herring (her.27.25-2932, SS3 3.30.22, 1903-2024): three runs that differ in
the time series of natural mortality by age (Run2 the highest M, Run3 the lowest), with B30 and F30 as the
model-internal benchmarks. The three reports ship in `extdata` (with the covariance reduced to the derived
quantities):

```{r ens-data}
her <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "her.27.25-2932", "her.27.25-2932.rds", package = "ss3diags2"))
names(her)
```

With equal weights each model contributes the same number of draws:

```{r ens, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 9}
ens <- ss3_ensemble(her, weights = c(1, 1, 1), iters = 1000)
attr(ens, "weights")
ss3plot_ensemble(ens, start = 1960)
```

With hypothetical weights 1.5, 1 and 0.5 (normalised to 0.5, 0.33 and 0.17) the joint ensemble moves towards Run1
and away from the low-M run:

```{r ens-w, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 9}
ensw <- ss3_ensemble(her, weights = c(1.5, 1, 0.5), iters = 1000)
attr(ensw, "weights")
ss3plot_ensemble(ensw, start = 1960)
```

The two joint ensembles on their own, and the Kobe plot of the equally weighted one:

```{r ens-joint, fig.height = 3.5, fig.width = 8}
ss3plot_trj(FLCore::FLStocks(equal = ens$Joint, weighted = ensw$Joint), type = c("B/Btgt", "F/Ftgt"))
```

```{r ens-kobe, fig.height = 4.5, fig.width = 6}
ss3plot_kobe(ens$Joint)
```

> **Weights and years.** Weights are normalised to sum to one; model $i$ contributes `round(iters * n * w_i)`
> draws. The joint ensemble covers the years common to all models. Models built from `FLStockR` with iterations
> (`ss3stk(output = "iters")`) are resampled to their number of draws.

> **Reading the ensemble.** The models agree on the trends but differ in scale: with higher M (Run2) the stock is
> more productive, so biomass is larger relative to B30 and F lower relative to F30; the low-M run (Run3) is the
> most pessimistic. The joint bands are wider than any single model's because they include the spread between
> models (structural uncertainty) as well as the estimation uncertainty within each. Down-weighting Run3 shifts the
> joint status towards the more optimistic runs, so weights should be justified (diagnostics, plausibility of M),
> not tuned to the outcome.
